P1:
On Jan 14, 2026 Roblox added an Async suffix to 46 yielding methods. The old names are deprecated for information only: they behave the same, still run, and are not scheduled for removal.
- Player:LoadCharacter -> Player:LoadCharacterAsync (old name still works).
- BadgeService:AwardBadge -> BadgeService:AwardBadgeAsync (old name still works).
- MarketplaceService:GetProductInfo -> MarketplaceService:GetProductInfoAsync (same arguments and return value; old name still works).
- Instance:WaitForChild: not renamed. Keep using WaitForChild.
- RemoteFunction:InvokeServer: not renamed. InvokeClient and BindableFunction:Invoke are also unchanged.
Use the Async names in new code.
P2:
- Turn it on: set Workspace.AuthorityMode = Server (full release July 9, 2026).
- It forces these settings: StreamingEnabled, NextGenerationReplication, PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem and UseFixedSimulation are all set to Enabled, and SignalBehavior is set to Deferred.
- Client-predicted gameplay logic goes in a function registered with RunService:BindToSimulation(fn). Put it in a ModuleScript that both the client and the server require, so the same code runs on both and can be rolled back and resimulated. Read input from InputAction objects (Input Action System), not from RemoteEvents, because remotes are not on the simulation timeline.
- Clock: use time() (simulation time) inside that logic, not os.clock or tick.
- Limits and gotchas: at most 64 predicted attributes, and names and strings are capped at 50 characters. Destroy and reparenting raise errors inside bound functions. Rendering and VFX go in RenderStepped and must tolerate rollback.
P3:
- Property: Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem.
- Timeline:
  - Phase 1 (June 2026): the default is Disabled and games opt in.
  - Phase 2 (planned for early 2027): the default becomes Enabled.
  - Phase 3 (planned for mid 2027): the property is removed and the old scripts are gone.

P5:
Since July 29, 2026, limits are calculated per experience and shared by all servers and Open Cloud:
- Write requests: 300 + 20 x CCU per minute.
- Read requests (standard or ordered): 300 + 40 x CCU per minute.
- List requests: 300 + 2 x CCU per minute.
- Remove requests: 300 + 40 x CCU per minute.
- The old base was 250.
- UpdateAsync costs one read and one write, so it draws from both budgets.
- Storage: 500 MB + 1 MB x lifetime players. Only the latest version of each key counts, measured compressed.
- Per-key throughput: 4 MB/min for writes and 25 MB/min for reads. Each request is rounded up to the next KB.
- Server budgets can be inspected with GetRequestBudgetForRequestType and lowered with SetRateLimitForRequestType.
- Open Cloud jobs use the same pool as live servers, so throttle bulk scripts.

- Gems bought with Robux make the crate a paid random item, even when a player earned their gems in play. Item bundles that include a random item also count.

  - Every possible outcome with its numeric odds, adding up to 100%.

G1:
Rules:
- Only one script may set MarketplaceService.ProcessReceipt. A second assignment silently replaces the first.
- Look up the player with GetPlayerByUserId(receipt.PlayerId). If the player is nil (not on this server), return NotProcessedYet.
- Make the callback idempotent by PurchaseId. The same receipt can be delivered more than once, so check whether this PurchaseId is already recorded before granting.
- Grant the item and record the PurchaseId in the same saved document (for example inside one UpdateAsync on the player's profile). The grant and the marker then succeed or fail together.
- Return PurchaseGranted only after that save succeeds. If the save, the product lookup or anything else fails, return NotProcessedYet so Roblox delivers the receipt again later.
- Do not yield between the grant and the marker. Use an in-flight guard per PurchaseId. Never grant from the client signal PromptProductPurchaseFinished.

Why players get charged and receive nothing: PurchaseGranted was returned before or despite a failed save, the player was missing, the profile failed to load, or a later stale save overwrote the grant. Roblox treats the purchase as done and never retries.

Why players receive an item twice: there is no PurchaseId check, the grant and the marker live in different stores so a crash between the two writes repeats the grant, or the grant happens in several places.
G2:
When to use which:
- SetAsync blindly overwrites the key. A concurrent or stale server can wipe newer data, for example after a teleport, a fast rejoin or a second server.
- Use UpdateAsync for player data whenever another server might write the key or you need read-modify-write. In practice that means always, together with a session lock.

Rules for the transform function:
- It receives (oldValue, keyInfo) and returns newValue, userIds, metadata. If you return only a value, the existing userIds and metadata are cleared, so pass through keyInfo:GetUserIds() and keyInfo:GetMetadata().
- It must not yield: no task.wait, no other Async calls, no remote invokes.
- It may run several times if another server wrote in between. Keep it pure, with no side effects such as grants, remotes or logs, and reset any flags at the start of each run.
- Return nil to cancel the write. The call still reports success, so check the result. Validate oldValue, including nil for a new player and the session lock owner, before changing it.
- UpdateAsync costs one read and one write of budget.
G3:
No, it is not safe.
- NaN passes the checks. typeof(0/0) is "number", and every comparison with NaN is false, so both bounds checks pass. inf also deserves a check.
- Fractional values such as 0.5 are allowed.
- It is a check-then-act race. Gold is not reserved or deducted, so the player can create many offers with the same gold, or spend it elsewhere before the trade completes. That is a duplication exploit.
- There is no rate limit and no check that the player is in a valid trade state.
- Gold lives in a client-visible Value. It is fine if only the server writes it, but the authoritative balance should be server data.

Fix:
```lua
offerRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, gold)
    if typeof(gold) ~= "number" or gold ~= gold or gold == math.huge then return end
    if gold % 1 ~= 0 or gold <= 0 then return end
    if not rateLimit(player) or not inTradeSession(player) then return end
    local data = getProfile(player)
    if not data or gold > data.Gold - data.EscrowedGold then return end
    data.EscrowedGold += gold -- reserve now; release on cancel; transfer atomically on accept
    createOffer(player, gold)
end)
```
When the trade is accepted, check both sides again and move the gold in one server-side step.
G4:
- Why: the Animator rewrites Motor6D.Transform on every joint that a playing track keys, every frame. Heartbeat runs after the Animator has already applied the pose, and on the next animation step your value is overwritten again. So the idle animation wins, and since the idle keys the barrel joint, your aim is wiped.
- Where to write: in RunService.PreSimulation (formerly Stepped), which runs after the Animator and before physics and rendering. Write every frame and compose with the animated value instead of replacing it:
  - motor.Transform = aimRot * motor.Transform applies the aim in the parent frame (look-at).
  - motor.Transform = motor.Transform * aimRot applies it inside the animation's frame.
- Joints that no track keys are not reset, so Transform = Transform * x compounds every frame. Keep your own base value, or restore it in PreAnimation. Skip extra layers when Animator.EvaluationThrottled is true.
- When to edit C0 (or C1) instead: for a static rest, mount or grip offset that should be permanent, isn't driven per frame, and that animations should play on top of. Use Transform for dynamic procedural offsets that must stack with clips.
G5:
- Priority is decided per joint, and a track only competes on joints it actually keys. The levels are Core < Idle < Movement < Action < Action2 < Action3 < Action4.
- The higher priority is applied first. If its total weight on that joint is 1, lower priorities get nothing there.
- Within the same priority, the tracks' weights are summed. If the sum is 1 or more, each track is scaled by w / sum. If the sum is below 1, the remaining weight goes to lower priorities.
- So a swing at Action with weight 1 fully overrides a walk at Movement on the right arm. If the swing is Movement (or Core), or has the same priority as the walk, the two blend, which makes the swing look weak. A swing with weight below 1 (for example 0.6) blends 60/40 with the walk underneath.
- Weight is set with AdjustWeight(weight, fadeTime) or Play(fadeTime, weight, speed). Fades ramp weight linearly. Total weight below 1 with nothing underneath drifts toward the rest pose.
- Fix: set the swing animation's Priority to Action (in the editor, or on the track before Play), keep weight 1, and make sure the swing keys the arm joints.
G6:
- Why: the unit chain doesn't match. Blender works in metres, FBX stores centimetres (unit scale 100), and Studio's importer reads the file in a different unit, so the model comes in at about 100x size (or 1/100). Scaling it down in Studio is a bad fix, because animation translations stay in the old units.
- Recommended FBX export from Blender:
  - Set Apply Scalings to "FBX Unit Scale" and leave every other scale at 1.0. Alternatively, set export scale to 0.01 or scene Unit Scale to 0.01, but use only one method.
  - Forward: -Z (or Z per rig convention), Up: Y. Apply Transform as needed. Apply all transforms in Blender first (Ctrl+A).
  - Rigs: turn Add Leaf Bones off, keep Key All Bones on, set Bake Simplify to 0, and turn Only Deform Bones on if the rig has control bones.
  - Check the importer's scale and unit options in Studio before you confirm the import.
- Alternative: GLB export has no unit-scale problem.
G7:
- Why: the glTF exporter's "Apply Modifiers" option (under Mesh in the export settings) is off by default. Without it, Mirror, Bevel and other modifiers are dropped and only the base mesh is exported, so you get half the model and sharp edges.
- Fix: turn on Apply Modifiers. It applies every modifier except Armature, so skinning still works.
- The catch: when Apply Modifiers is on, the exporter does not export shape keys (morph targets). For meshes with shape keys, apply the Mirror and Bevel modifiers manually in Blender instead (shape keys can block that, which needs a workaround), or drop the shape keys.
- Also keep modifier order and auto-smooth or custom normals in mind, so bevel shading survives the export.
G8:
- Stretching: fromScale(0.3, 0.3) is 30% of the safe-area width and 30% of its height. Screens have different aspect ratios, so the frame is a different shape on each one. Fix: add a UIAspectRatioConstraint (for example AspectRatio = 1). Optionally add a UISizeConstraint for minimum and maximum size, and one UIScale per screen.
- Notch and top bar: content placed at (0,0) can land under the notch, camera cutout or Roblox top bar.
  - Put interactive UI in a ScreenGui with ScreenInsets = Enum.ScreenInsets.CoreUISafeInsets (the default and recommended choice). It keeps content clear of both the device cutouts and the core top bar.
  - DeviceSafeInsets avoids only the notch. TopbarSafeInsets is for custom rows in the top bar.
  - Do not set ScreenInsets = None or IgnoreGuiInset on interactive UI.
  - Do not hard-code the top-bar height or read GuiService.TopbarInset only once at startup.
- Full-screen art belongs in a separate ScreenGui with ScreenInsets = None and SafeAreaCompatibility = None, with no buttons inside it.

```lua
local RS = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local Items = require(game.ServerStorage.ItemCatalog) -- [id] = {Price=..., MaxQty=...}
local Data = require(game.ServerScriptService.PlayerData)
local BuyItem = RS.Remotes.BuyItem
local last = {}

BuyItem.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, itemId, quantity)
    local now = os.clock()
    if last[player] and now - last[player] < 0.5 then return end -- rate limit
    last[player] = now
    if typeof(itemId) ~= "string" or #itemId > 50 then return end
    if typeof(quantity) ~= "number" or quantity ~= quantity
        or quantity % 1 ~= 0 or quantity < 1 then return end
    local item = Items[itemId]
    if not item then return end
    quantity = math.min(quantity, item.MaxQty or 99)
    local profile = Data.get(player)
    if not profile then return end
    local cost = item.Price * quantity -- price from the server, never the client
    if profile.Coins < cost then return end
    profile.Coins -= cost -- no yield between check and write
    profile.Inventory[itemId] = (profile.Inventory[itemId] or 0) + quantity
end)
game:GetService("Players").PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p) last[p] = nil end)
```
The server validates types, rejects NaN and fractions, owns prices and balances, deducts atomically, rate limits, and cleans up per-player state.
T2:
```lua
-- Load and lock in one UpdateAsync
local function load(player)
  local session = game.JobId .. ":" .. HttpService:GenerateGUID(false)
  for attempt = 1, 5 do
    local ok, data = pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, key(player), function(old)
      old = old or defaults()
      local lock = old.Lock
      if lock and lock.Session ~= session and os.time() - lock.Time < LEASE then
        return nil -- locked by another server: cancel the write
      end
      old.Lock = {Session = session, Time = os.time()}
      return old
    end)
    if ok and data and data.Lock and data.Lock.Session == session then
      return data, session -- ready
    end
    task.wait(2 ^ attempt) -- locked or error: wait for the other server to release (or the lease to expire)
  end
  player:Kick("Data busy, rejoin") -- never play on default data
end

-- Every save is fenced by the session token
local function save(player, release)
  store:UpdateAsync(key(player), function(old)
    if not old or not old.Lock or old.Lock.Session ~= sessions[player] then
      return nil -- lock lost: refuse the write
    end
    local new = serialize(profiles[player])
    new.Lock = (not release) and {Session = sessions[player], Time = os.time()} or nil
    return new
  end)
end
```
- Autosave every 60-120 s renews the lease. The lease lasts about 2-3 autosave periods.
- PlayerRemoving calls save(player, true) to release the lock. BindToClose saves everyone in parallel.
- Before teleporting, save and release the lock. The destination server waits or retries until the lock is free.
- Run trades and purchases inside the same profile save, with idempotent PurchaseIds.

T4:
Diagnosis: FireServer automatically passes the sending player as the first argument of OnServerEvent. The client also passed LocalPlayer, so on the server player is the real sender, amount is the Player instance (the extra argument), and 50 arrives as a third argument. amount + 1 then fails with "arithmetic on a Instance value".

Fix: never pass the local player yourself.
```lua
-- client
remote:FireServer(50)
-- server
remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, amount)
    if typeof(amount) ~= "number" or amount ~= amount then return end
    print(amount + 1)
end)
```
Also validate amount on the server and never trust identity from client arguments. Use the automatic player parameter.
T5:
Why: in Studio solo play the local player often joins before the server Script finishes loading and reaches the PlayerAdded:Connect line, for example after a require or a WaitForChild that yields first. PlayerAdded has already fired for that player, so the handler never runs. Live servers usually start before anyone joins, which hides the race.

Standard fix: connect the handler, then loop over the players who are already in the game.
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local function onPlayerAdded(player)
    local ls = Instance.new("Folder")
    ls.Name = "leaderstats"
    local coins = Instance.new("IntValue")
    coins.Name = "Coins"
    coins.Parent = ls
    ls.Parent = player
end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayerAdded)
for _, p in Players:GetPlayers() do
    task.spawn(onPlayerAdded, p)
end
```
Connect before any yields, and make the handler safe to run twice.

T8:
Most likely, Workspace.MeshStreamingAndImprovedLoDs is Enabled (or turned on by default in the published game). In that mode every mesh uses cloud-generated LoDs and mesh streaming, and MeshPart.RenderFidelity is ignored, so setting Precise has no effect. The RenderFidelity property is planned for removal.

What to do:
- Check the Workspace property (Default / Enabled / Disabled).
- With the new system on, you control detail at the source: give hero meshes a sensible triangle budget (at most 20,000 per mesh) and split heavy objects into several meshes. You cannot force full detail at distance.
- If you disable it (while still possible), RenderFidelity works again. Automatic means highest detail under 250 studs, medium from 250 to 500, and lowest beyond 500. Precise always uses the highest detail but costs performance.
- Also check that the published place actually has the property saved, and that you are not looking at Studio-only settings.
